title: NSE Market Regime Classifier
summary: Classifies NIFTY market regimes using trend and volatility features.

title: Logistic Regression
summary: Estimates the probability that a borrower defaults and classifies them as likely to repay or default.

charts.caption: ROC curve on held-out data: how well the model ranks risky borrowers above safe ones.
Confusion matrix on held-out data at a 0.5 probability threshold.
Learned coefficients: positive values push the prediction toward default.
Calibration: predicted probabilities against the default rate actually observed.

title: Linear Regression
summary: Predicts a stock's daily return from the market's move, its sector's move and trading volume.

charts.caption: Predicted against actual daily returns on held-out data.
Residuals show no pattern, which suggests a straight line is a reasonable fit.
Learned coefficients: the market return coefficient is the stock's beta.
Residuals are roughly bell-shaped and centred on zero.

title: Decision Tree
summary: Decides whether a loan application is approved using a short tree of yes/no questions you can read.

charts.caption: The learned tree (top two levels): each box is a yes/no question about the applicant.
Which questions the tree relies on most when deciding.
Deeper trees memorise the training data; held-out accuracy stops improving early.
Confusion matrix on held-out data.

title: Random Forest
summary: Predicts a stock's 30-day volatility from beta, leverage, size and sector with an ensemble of decision trees.

charts.caption: Predicted against actual volatility on held-out stocks.
Which inputs the forest relies on most to predict volatility.
Same data, same inputs: the forest captures effects a straight line misses.
Predicted volatility as beta rises, other inputs held typical. The slope differs by sector.

title: Support Vector Machine
summary: Estimates the probability that a card transaction is fraud using an RBF support vector machine.

charts.caption: Fraud probability across amount and distance for a 3am online purchase; the line marks 50%.
ROC curve on held-out transactions.
How cleanly predicted fraud probabilities separate the two groups.
Confusion matrix on held-out data.

title: k-Nearest Neighbours
summary: Classifies a stock as Value, Growth or Income by finding the most similar stocks.

charts.caption: Held-out stocks by P/E and revenue growth. Value and Income overlap, Growth stands apart.
With k=1 the model memorises noise; a moderate k generalises better.
Confusion matrix on held-out data.

title: Naive Bayes
summary: Estimates the chance that a bank customer leaves from age, balance, products, tenure and activity.

charts.caption: Naive Bayes models each feature's distribution per class; these are the shapes it compares.
ROC curve on held-out customers.
Naive Bayes is often over-confident: probabilities drift from observed rates.
Confusion matrix on held-out data.
